steps.message:
Before I write it: this is a destructive, non-reversible change, so I want a yes first.

Dropping `users.notes` permanently deletes the contents of that column for all 48,000 production rows the moment the deploy job applies the migration. SQLite's `DROP COLUMN` has no down-migration that can bring the data back — a rollback would restore the column empty. Your note that "we stopped using it" tells me nothing currently reads it, which is a different thing from nobody ever wanting it back; nothing in this repo references `notes` outside `schema.sql` and `001_create_users.sql`, so I can't verify that from the code either.

questions.question: Dropping `users.notes` destroys that data for 48,000 production rows with no way to restore it. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Archive first, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 copies notes into a `users_notes_archive` table (or an export) before the ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN. Keeps the data recoverable; slightly more than 'just the drop'.

options.label: Yes, drop it outright
options.description: Migration 003 is a single `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;` plus the matching edit to schema.sql. The notes data is gone permanently on deploy.

options.label: Don't drop yet
options.description: Leave the column in place and stop at deprecating it (e.g. a comment in schema.sql), so the data stays until you're certain.

Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — a single `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the mirrored schema stays in sync.

Two things worth knowing before the deploy job runs it:

- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35.0 or newer (2021-03). On an older engine the migration errors out rather than silently doing nothing.
- No down-migration exists, per your call. Nothing is committed — `git status` shows both files as uncommitted changes.
